subject: Recap + Next Steps: ClearPath AI model-fit & benchmarking artifacts
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <sam@clearpath-ai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + Next Steps: ClearPath AI model-fit & benchmarking artifacts

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the scope for a short model-fit run on Redwood: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary use case: extract structured diagnostic codes and short physician-recommendation snippets from outpatient visit notes (sensitive PHI, low-latency path).
- Target throughput: ~50 qps peak for batch inference during nightly runs; production latency SLO for interactive UI ~300ms p95.
- Success criteria: precision on key fields >= 0.92, semantic similarity for recommendations >= 0.85 vs clinician gold, and no quality regressions vs current rule-based baseline.

What Redwood recommends for an initial bench: 
- Models to try: redwood/llama-3-13b-q4f (fast quantized 13B), redwood/opt-6.7b-int8 (lower-cost baseline), and redwood/rlhf-instruct-7b (safety-oriented).
- Prompt sets: clinical_struct_extract_v1 (field extraction), recommendation_gen_v2 (recommendation paraphrase + conservative tone). I'll attach the prompt set examples.
- Dataset format: CSV with columns [id,input_text,expected_json,split,notes]. See attached sample (clearpath_eval_dataset.csv).
- Scoring: automated exact-match for codes, BERTScore/embedding sim for free-text with threshold 0.85, and a human-review bucket for any item with model_confidence < 0.6.

Next steps I propose (timeline):
1) You share a representative sample of ~1k de-identified notes (or s3/drive link) by Mon 3/16. (Procurement loop welcomed for DPA/transfer).
2) We run 3 model variants across the sample and produce a per-model scoring report (2–3 business days after upload).
3) Joint review call to go over failure modes and rollout recommendations.

Attachments: clearpath_eval_dataset.csv (sample), redwood_eval_template.jsonl (scoring template), pricing_onepager.pdf

If that all looks good, I can open the eval run and share a Redwood Console link where you can monitor token breakdown and per-route latency.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Samir Shah <sam@clearpath-ai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + Next Steps: ClearPath AI model-fit & benchmarking artifacts

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the concise plan. Quick answers from our side: 

- We can provide 1,200 de-identified notes by end of day Monday (we'll anonymize PHI to the spec). I'll share via a secure GDrive folder and drop access to procurement@clearpath-ai.com.
- For compliance: we need confirmation of data-at-rest encryption and retention policy for eval artifacts. Can you confirm the default retention on Redwood eval uploads and whether we can set a 30-day auto-delete?
- Also: do you have recommended temperature/decoding configs for the recommendation_gen prompts (we want conservative language)?

If you can confirm the above, we'll go ahead and upload. Also cc'd procurement to start DPA discussion.

Samir Shah
Head of Product, ClearPath AI
sam@clearpath-ai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap + Next Steps: ClearPath AI model-fit & benchmarking artifacts

On Fri, Mar 13, 2026 at 09:06 AM Samir Shah <sam@clearpath-ai.com> wrote:
> For compliance: we need confirmation of data-at-rest encryption and retention policy for eval artifacts. Can you confirm the default retention on Redwood eval uploads and whether we can set a 30-day auto-delete?

Quick internal note for the run and reply draft to Samir: 
- Data handling: Redwood eval storage uses AES-256 at rest; customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments. For hosted eval uploads, default retention is 90 days but we can set a per-run TTL — engineering can set a 30-day auto-delete flag on the eval job (we've used this with other enterprise customers).
- Access control: Make sure Share settings are limited; we'll create a dedicated eval workspace for ClearPath with RBAC so only their org and the assigned SEs can view.
- Decoding/prompting recs for recommendation_gen_v2: temp 0.0–0.2, top_p 0.85, max_tokens 80, deterministic sampling for extraction prompts (greedy).
- Evaluation pipeline: run three model variants; compute exact-match for structured fields (codes), micro-F1 for multi-label where applicable, embedding-similarity for text (use sentence-transformers-sim with threshold 0.85). Anything below threshold goes to human-review queue.

I'll take the lead on the security confirmation email. Priyom — draft reply to Samir with these bullet answers and ask them to share the drive link + confirm the de-id approach. I can loop Legal if procurement requests DPA language.

Ben
Head of Solution Architecture | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <sam@clearpath-ai.com>, procurement@clearpath-ai.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + Next Steps: ClearPath AI model-fit & benchmarking artifacts

Samir — sounds good, thanks. Short answers inline and next actions: 

- Encryption & retention: Hosted eval uploads are encrypted AES-256 at rest; we support customer KMS for Private deployments. Default retention is 90 days but we can set a 30-day TTL for this eval run. I'll enable the TTL and confirm when the job is created.
- De-identification: your plan to remove PHI fields + hash patient IDs is fine for the quick benchmark. Please include a short README (columns and de-id steps) in the Drive folder.
- Prompt/decoding: for recommendation_gen_v2 use temperature=0.1, top_p=0.85, max_tokens=80, presence_penalty=0. Priority is conservative language and high precision. For extraction prompts run greedy decoding (deterministic).

Action items:
- Samir: share the GDrive link for the 1.2k sample and the README by EOD Mon 3/16. Procurement: happy to start DPA review; Ben will loop Legal if needed.
- Redwood: we'll create the eval run (note: this will create a temporary results bucket with 30-day TTL), run the three model variants, and circulate a report with per-field precision/recall, embedding similarity distribution, and failure examples within 48 hours of dataset upload.

I'll upload the redwood_eval_template.jsonl and the scoring rubric to the shared Drive once you grant access. Looking forward to the run — if anything changes, flag it in this thread.

Best,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

(Attachment stubs: clearpath_eval_dataset.csv, redwood_eval_template.jsonl, pricing_onepager.pdf)
